projects.name: WayneUI
projects.role: The interface layer: brand tokens, CSS, Vue, Blade and raw-PHP components, and a runnable accessibility gate. Four consumer paths that must agree: static HTML, raw PHP, Laravel with Blade, and Vue (SPA or Inertia).
projects.next_step: Build every screen from its components; read its markup contract before writing markup by hand.

projects.name: CREED
projects.role: The handbook and policy.json (support dates per runtime). Every other project reads its policy; it is the one place that decides what state a version is in.
projects.next_step: Read the handbook chapter for the area you are changing; use policy_lookup for dates.

projects.name: PROCTOR
projects.role: One command that measures a PHP app against policy.json and prints a JSON, text or Code Quality report. It reports; CI decides.
projects.next_step: Run run_proctor_check on the app, fix the failing checks, and keep `proctor check` in CI.

projects.name: SESAME
projects.role: Protocol-neutral sign-in: drivers for CAS, a signed gateway assertion, OpenID Connect (Entra sign-in) and OAuth2 bearer tokens (SAML is planned). It returns a verified identity and leaves the session to the app.
projects.next_step: Pick the driver your platform supports and read its README before wiring routes.

projects.name: HELMET
projects.role: The runtime baseline: security headers, CSP, session hardening, trusted proxies, a health check and a version warning.
projects.next_step: Add it as a dependency and start from its presets; it reads the same policy as PROCTOR.

projects.name: Sourdough
projects.role: The starters: one command generates a new app in the shape you pick: raw PHP (`sourdough new --raw`), raw PHP with a Vue SPA (`--raw --vue`), Laravel with Blade (`--laravel`), Laravel with Blade and Vue islands (`--laravel --vue`) or Laravel with Inertia and Vue (`--inertia`). `--sail` or `--docker` adds a local runtime to the Laravel shapes.
projects.next_step: Start a new app with `sourdough new` and the shape flag you need; keep an app honest with `sourdough manifest --check`, and bring template updates in with `sourdough feed`.

projects.name: Preflight
projects.role: CI templates for GitLab (components) and GitHub (reusable workflows): tests, PROCTOR, audit and accessibility, with `composer ci` as the one contract.
projects.next_step: Include its components pinned to a tag; never track the latest.

projects.name: Pinstripe
projects.role: The coding standard: shared Pint and PHPStan presets, plus ESLint and Prettier configuration.
projects.next_step: Point Pint and PHPStan at its presets; one formatter per repository.

projects.name: Booster
projects.role: The upgrade tool: Rector recipes and checks that move an app one PHP or Laravel version at a time.
projects.next_step: Plan one hop at a time with `upgrade_path`, and read its README for the Rector recipes.

projects.name: Rollcall
projects.role: The fleet census: PHP, image, framework and PROCTOR result for every app, and the end-of-life burn-down.
projects.next_step: Owners check their app's row; a missing row means the app is not registered.

projects.name: Drawbridge
projects.role: The Citadel auth gateway: one OpenID Connect client through Entra ID that hands each app a signed assertion for SESAME's gateway driver.
projects.next_step: Apps on Citadel use SESAME's gateway driver; plan against the Drawbridge README.

projects.name: Squire
projects.role: The Citadel kit: build.sh, deployments/, the app-side release script, the health check, the portable image and upstream merge requests. Platform-specific deploy code lives here and nowhere else. Its old local parity kit gives way to Parity.
projects.next_step: Use its release script for Citadel deploys; other platforms use their own targets. To run the app like Citadel on your own computer, use Parity.

projects.name: Parity
projects.role: Runs Citadel on your own computer: Citadel's own PHP image, Citadel's proxy and MySQL 5.6, for any app, with or without Squire. One Go command line for Windows, macOS and Linux (an optional desktop app follows), on Docker or Podman, with Podman recommended. Commands: check, init, up, down, status, logs, shell, image and test. It is the stack's local-development answer and replaces Squire's parity group.
projects.next_step: Install a release from its repository on git.wayne.edu (enterprise-apps/parity; 0.1.0 release candidates so far, with Windows, macOS and Linux archives), then run `parity check`, `parity init` and `parity up` in the app's folder. Coming from Squire's parity kit: `parity init --from-squire`.

projects.name: ADVISOR
projects.role: This server: orients a developer and gives their coding agent read-only tools into the stack. It sits beside Laravel Boost and does not replace it.
projects.next_step: Run `advisor install` to wire your agent, then start with list_projects.

projects.name: WELD
projects.role: Wired, Everything, Linked, Deployed: one Laravel + Inertia/Vue app with every stack part already joined. A team clones it, renames it and deploys it.
projects.next_step: Clone it for a new Laravel + Inertia/Vue app; its front page shows how the parts fit.
